rgb: The view shows the corner of an indoor room, with a tiered wall shelf on the left wall approximately 1.5 to 2.5 metres ahead of the camera wearer and a barred window on the right wall around 1.5 to 2.5 metres away. Three shirtless men in dark lower garments are visible: one stands at the front-left roughly 0.8 to 1.2 metres in front of the camera wearer, another stands at the extreme right edge about 0.8 to 1.2 metres away, and the third is farther back near the corner between the shelf and window, about 1.8 to 2.2 metres from the camera wearer and approximately 1.0 to 1.5 metres from the other two. The front-left man faces away and slightly right toward the shelf, holding a small open booklet within arm's reach; the far-right man is shown in left-facing profile; and the rear man faces left toward the shelf, carrying a plate of red flowers in his left hand while remaining within arm's reach of the shelf's framed picture and lit lamps. None of them looks toward the camera wearer. Both foreground men are within the camera wearer's arm's reach and are cropped below the chest or waist by the lower frame edge. In frames 2, 4, and 5, most of the far-right man's head and torso lies outside the right edge, while the front-left man's body partly blocks the shelf's lower-left area and a red bag hanging behind him. Through the five frames, the viewpoint moves slightly left and right: frames 1 and 3 reveal more of the barred window and the far-right man's face, whereas frames 2, 4, and 5 show more of the left wall and a hanging blue bag. Meanwhile, the rear man withdraws his right arm from its shelf-level extension in frames 1–3 back toward the plate in his left hand in frames 4–5, and the far-right man moves his hands slightly forward in frame 5.
depth: The depth representation depicts the three-dimensional structure of a small room corner, including a recessed, multi-level altar on the left wall, a barred window on the right wall, and three men positioned at separate depth levels. The booklet-holding man in the left foreground and the man cropped along the right foreground edge appear very bright; both are within arm's reach of the camera wearer at about 0.6 to 1.0 metres, with roughly 1.0 to 1.2 metres between them. A third man occupies the centre-right farther back at approximately 1.8 to 2.2 metres, around 1.2 metres beyond the foreground pair. Over the 5 frames, the left foreground man remains turned away and slightly right toward the altar while edging a little closer to the camera. The right foreground man faces left, but in frames 2, 4, and 5 his head and body are mostly outside the image, leaving only his hands at the bottom-right. The background man faces left toward the altar, holds a tray of red petals in his left hand, and has the shelf objects within arm's reach. None of the men looks toward the camera wearer. Relative to the RGB strip, the depth map more clearly exposes the smooth distance gradient running along the side walls, the recessed progression of the altar shelves, and the strong depth gap between the foreground men's shoulders and the man behind them. Its estimates are unreliable, however, within the altar's dark recess, where the lit flames and reflective brass vessels collapse into evenly dark regions, and around slender features such as the window bars and the right foreground man's fingers, which smear into nearby background depths.
segmentation: The instance-segmentation view extracts the foreground and midground people as separate two-dimensional silhouettes on black, distinguishing the left foreground man, about 0.7 to 0.9 metres away and cropped below the upper back; the centre-right standing man, roughly 2.0 metres away and cropped below the knees; and the right-edge man, around 0.8 metres away and heavily occluded by the right image boundary. Across the 5 frames, the masks place the left man at the front-left, facing away-right and partly covering the lower altar shelf. They show the background man standing in the front-centre and facing left, with his right arm extended toward the shelf in frames 1 to 3 before he draws it back to his tray in frames 4 to 5. The right-side man appears with a torso and head in frames 1 and 3, vanishes entirely in frames 2 and 5, and becomes only a lower-corner mask in frame 4. The map gives clean boundary outlines between overlapping people and identifies small carried or wall-mounted items within the participants' arm's reach, including the small booklet in the left man's hands in frame 1, the red bag hanging at the far-left wall edge in frame 2, and the background man's waist-high tray in frame 1, but it provides no direct distance measurements without the RGB context. Its class assignments and frame-to-frame consistency are also highly unreliable: the booklet is wrongly labelled a 'cell phone', the flower tray a 'pizza', and the hanging wall bag a 'handbag'. The barred-window wall on the right is misidentified as a 'refrigerator' in frames 1 and 4 and as an 'oven' in frame 3. In addition, several frames lose every object and background mask, and the right-edge man's hands are absent in frames 2 and 5.
pose: The body-and-hand skeleton display draws sparse two-dimensional joints and connecting bones over a black field, recording the torso, arm positions, and facial-profile direction of the centre-right standing man about 2.0 metres away, along with isolated keypoints from the nearer men, approximately 0.6 to 1.0 metres away, whenever they are detected. In frames 3 and 5, the background man's yellow upper-body skeleton traces shoulders, elbows, and wrists directed leftward, while his head keypoints point left and down toward the tray held within his arm's reach. This confirms that he never looks at the camera wearer. Magenta hand meshes resolve detailed finger articulation for the background man's right hand in the centre of frame 2 and for the right-foreground man's clasped hands at the bottom-right of frame 5. Compared with the RGB view, these skeletal overlays make the joint angles, torso lean, and overlapping finger arrangements explicit without interference from lighting clutter or skin-tone merging. Even so, the map is exceptionally sparse and inconsistent throughout the sequence: frame 4 detects none of the three people; frames 1 and 2 omit the background man's body; and the left foreground man is not tracked apart from a broken head-and-shoulder group in frame 1 because he is cropped and has his back turned. The representation also leaves out the complete room geometry, the altar shelving, and all held objects.
